scope: Epoch 4 Registry, cross-platform, security, and release evidence
observations: A Registry record must preserve source harness, privacy, lineage, portability level, and digest-bound evidence; registration must never turn a private artifact into a public download.
Cross-platform equivalence must compare semantic and native layer digests, not whole archive bytes when created_at truthfully differs.
CRLF/LF fixture drift can masquerade as state-portability drift; explicit UTF-8 LF test inputs remove that confound without altering real source data.
A structured secret scanner that treats malformed JSON, YAML, JSONL, or TOML as clean is fail-open; unparseable declared structured data must fail closed.
Rollback evidence is materially stronger when a real host creates and recognizes the target before deterministic failure injection, then the same real host verifies cleanup.
Configured hosted CI is not observed cross-platform evidence until the workflow actually runs.
Wheel and sdist claims require separate fresh-environment installs; build-backend and runtime dependency caches are different reproducibility concerns.
release_implications: Epoch 4 satisfies the local Registry and hardening gates and leaves a reproducible v0.1.0-beta.1 candidate.
Seven of eight Human Final Review questions pass; the negative trained-agent Gate E keeps question seven red and forbids rc.1 and v0.1.0.
No public repository, remote, push, or new tag is authorized or required for the local beta handoff.
